{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-oh-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"efefa1a34356e8a47c8d8c80b9f831ea7c562a7c1d35893ee2323772abc561c5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-oh-class-d:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"33124b165dc74fabcff4bbcd8fd15db36bbe4a69a10e7def76a9d71752a5128b","source_liveness_sha256":null},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"State laws and penalties","heading":"State laws and penalties — C2","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A51
A first over-limit chemical test carries a three-month, or ninety-day, license suspension in the listed schedule. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A51
An over-limit test with one prior impaired-driving or drug conviction carries a one-year license suspension in the listed schedule. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A51
An over-limit test with two prior impaired-driving or drug convictions carries a two-year license suspension in the listed schedule. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A51
An over-limit test with at least three prior impaired-driving or drug convictions carries a three-year license suspension in the listed schedule. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A51
At least five impaired-driving convictions in the preceding twenty years bring jail time and placement on Ohio's habitual impaired-driving offender registry, with possible vehicle immobilization or forfeiture. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A51
Before taking a nonprescription drug, read its warning label or ask a doctor or pharmacist about side effects that may affect driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A51
Prescription antidepressants, pain medicines, sleep aids and sedatives can affect safe driving, so check their warnings or ask a doctor or pharmacist about side effects. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A51
Illegal drugs affect reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness and must never be used while driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A51
Never mix alcohol with other impairing drugs because drugs can intensify alcohol's effects or add separate effects. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A52
Courts assign license penalty points according to the traffic violation and applicable repeat violations. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A52
Accumulating six points within two years causes the Bureau to send a warning letter. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A52
Accumulating at least twelve points within two years causes a license suspension. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A52
Reinstatement after a twelve-point suspension requires steps that include a remedial course, a financial-responsibility filing with the Bureau and reinstatement fees. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A52
An S R twenty-two is a certificate filed with the state to show the auto policy meets minimum liability coverage, rather than a separate kind of insurance. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A52
Moving violations, certain speeding offenses and restriction violations are listed as two-point violations. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A52
Willful or wanton disregard for the safety of people or property is listed as a four-point violation. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A52
Failure to stop and identify yourself after a crash is among the listed six-point violations. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A52
For a driver younger than eighteen, convictions or guilty pleas for two moving violations trigger an automatic three-month license suspension. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A52
For a driver younger than eighteen, convictions or guilty pleas for three moving violations trigger an automatic one-year license suspension. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A52
For a driver younger than eighteen, conviction or a guilty plea for probationary impaired operation triggers a six-month license suspension. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A53
After the described probationary suspension, reinstatement includes obtaining a temporary instruction permit, completing an approved juvenile improvement program and passing the driving examination. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A53
Driving with a suspended license is a first-degree misdemeanor and, on conviction, can bring a fine up to one thousand dollars and another one-year suspension. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A53
An owner who knowingly lets a suspended driver use the vehicle may face the same penalty as that driver. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A53
Do not cling to or ride on the outside of a motor vehicle while it is moving. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A53
A driver must not knowingly carry someone younger than sixteen in an open or unroofed truck, trailer or semitrailer cargo area above twenty-five miles per hour unless a stated exception applies. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A53
The open-cargo-area restriction has an exception for a properly secured seat and a safety belt meeting federal restraint standards. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A53
The open-cargo-area restriction has an exception for an emergency threatening the life of the driver or the transported person. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A53
The open-cargo-area restriction has an exception for workers doing specialized street or highway maintenance or construction under public-agency authority. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A53
Use a child safety seat meeting federal motor-vehicle safety standards, installed properly and used according to its manufacturer's instructions. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A53
Never put a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger air bag. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R31 | anchor: A54
Children younger than four or weighing less than forty pounds, including those meeting both conditions, need a suitable federally compliant child seat in vehicles subject to the stated restraint law. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R32 | anchor: A54
In vehicles subject to the stated restraint law, a child at least four but younger than eight needs a booster unless at least four feet nine inches tall. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R33 | anchor: A54
The child-restraint body text states a safety-belt requirement from age eight through age fifteen in covered motor vehicles. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R34 | anchor: A54
Children twelve or younger should ride in the back seat to reduce air-bag injury risk during a crash. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R35 | anchor: A54
The listed child-restraint exemptions include public-safety vehicles, taxicabs and vehicles that did not legally need safety belts when manufactured. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-R36 | anchor: A54
Read both the vehicle manual and the child-restraint directions for information specific to the restraint system. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0054]

Confusables: a chemical-test refusal suspension can survive acquittal; financial-responsibility proof is distinct from a separate type of insurance. A child who meets either the younger-age or lighter-weight condition needs the stated child seat. Mnemonic: coverage, conduct, consequences. Glossary: administrative suspension is the described immediate license action; a booster and child seat serve different listed categories. These terms summarize the cited rules only.
